subject: Physics
exam_context: NEET UG 2026 - Physics section only, 50 questions printed (35 compulsory + 15 choice-of-10) / 45 scored questions / 180 marks
data_provenance: Estimated from PYQ-trend analysis and chapter-wise-weightage trackers aggregated across 2025 and 2026 NEET sessions (including the 21 June 2026 Re-NEET UG), not official NTA data; last grounded Sep 2026. Individual-session weightage varies, treat as multi-session averages for question-bank planning, not a guarantee of any single paper's composition.

P01.notes: Short, direct recall/formula unit; rarely more than 1 question.

P02.notes: One of the top-ranked Class 11 chapters by trend trackers; projectile-motion and relative-velocity numericals recur.

P03.approx_weightage_pct: 7 (combined with Work, Energy, Power and Rotational Motion in some trackers)
P03.notes: Friction and circular-motion (banking of roads) problems are a recurring archetype.

P04.notes: Collision numericals are a recurring, formula-driven favourite.

P05.chapter: Motion of System of Particles and Rigid Body
P05.notes: Grouped with Mechanics as a high-weightage bloc; moment-of-inertia numericals recur.

P06.notes: Escape velocity / orbital velocity numericals are the most common archetype.

P07.notes: Broad unit spanning elasticity, fluids and thermal properties; usually 1 question each from 2-3 sub-areas.

P09.chapter: Behaviour of Perfect Gas and Kinetic Theory
P09.notes: rms-speed / degrees-of-freedom numericals, often conceptually paired with Thermodynamics.

P10.notes: SHM energy/time-period numericals and standing-wave/beats questions recur.

P11.notes: Gauss's-law applications and capacitor-combination numericals recur.

P12.notes: Consistently a top-ranked Physics chapter; Wheatstone-bridge, meter-bridge and Kirchhoff's-law numericals recur.

P13.chapter: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
P13.notes: Biot-Savart/Ampere's-law numericals and moving-coil-galvanometer conversions recur often.

P14.notes: EMI and LCR-resonance numericals are a recurring archetype.

P15.notes: Mostly conceptual recall (spectrum identification, E/B/c relations); rarely more than one question.

P16.notes: Combines Ray and Wave Optics; among the highest-weightage Physics chapters, flagged across multiple 2026 trackers.

P17.chapter: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
P17.notes: Photoelectric-effect stopping-potential numericals are the dominant archetype.

P18.notes: Bohr-model transitions and radioactive-decay numericals recur.

P19.notes: Diode I-V characteristics and logic-gate truth tables are direct, NCERT-diagram-based questions with a rising-weightage trend.

broad_category_weightage_pct.note: Coarser cross-check figures, approximate % share of the 45-question scored Physics section, synthesised from multiple 2025-2026 PYQ trend sources. Rounds do not sum exactly to 100% because some marginal units are reported inconsistently across trackers.
broad_category_weightage_pct.Class_11_vs_Class_12_split: approx. 43-46% Class 11, 54-57% Class 12 across most trackers

marking_scheme.source_note: Confirmed via multiple Sep 2026 sources reporting on the 2026 and Re-NEET UG 2026 (21 June 2026) sessions.
marking_scheme.section_a: 35 single-correct MCQs, all compulsory; +4 for a correct answer, -1 for an incorrect answer, 0 if unattempted.
marking_scheme.section_b: 15 single-correct MCQs, attempt any 10 (if more than 10 are attempted, only the first 10 attempted, per answer sheet order, are evaluated in the official pattern used since 2021); +4 correct, -1 incorrect, 0 unattempted.
marking_scheme.question_types_used: Single-correct MCQ only. NEET does NOT use numerical-value, multiple-correct, or matrix-match formats — those are JEE-exclusive.
